licensure.disciplinary_grounds.rationale: These nine buckets map cleanly onto the dominant clusters visible across states: fraud/deceit in obtaining or using a license; incompetent or negligent workmanship; criminal convictions; violations of statutes, codes, or board rules; unlicensed practice, license lending, or acting beyond scope; contract abandonment, fund diversion, and failure to pay; insurance/bond/financial-responsibility failures; procedural failures (records, permits, notifications, continuing education); and reciprocal discipline from other jurisdictions—together covering every item without leaving a meaningful residual.

profession_specific.license_tiers.rationale: These eight buckets capture the dominant axes of variation: career-progression level (apprentice → journeyman → master), business-entity status (contractor), scope restrictions (residential-only, specialty/limited/low-voltage), oversight roles (inspector, administrator), and the broader general/engineering contractor class used by states like AZ, CA, and NV that license electricians under a general contractor framework.
